items.title: Tom McIntosh — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’ve never seen that girl since. I always wanted to give that girl a call... I lament that I have never seen Jeanie Olham, the girl that sent me to Juilliard. I never saw her since.

ctx.x: So, I caught up with her and I said, “Hi, how are you doing?” I became aggressive, “What’s you name.” “Jeanie Olham.” Boy, what a strange name. I thought, I’d accept that beautiful girl and I could see that she’s very intelligent. I said that I have to appear intelligent. So I said, “You’re starting to graduate now, what are you going to be doing with your life?” She says, “I’m going to Juilliard.” I had never heard

of Juilliard. She saw that and she said, “Oh, Juilliard is the best music school in the country.” I said, “Oh, thank you.” I mention this because when I went to the Army and things started to look up and I’m starting to improve as a musician, I started getting right. There was a war officer who tested everybody, and he thought I was the best in the band. The next thing, I went corporal to buck sergeant, to this then ultimately master sergeant. So, but do you want your life to say you spent 20 years in the Army…
